clue.text: Vessel crosses the bar ?

parts.note: reads as a ship sailing over a sandbar at a harbour mouth, but the vessel is also a tall glass handed across the counter of a pub

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests the sandbar a sailing ship crosses; it is also the pub counter over which this large sherry or beer glass is passed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a fore-and-aft rigged sailing ship and a large drinking glass, two kinds of vessel.

clue.text: One's in a -sort of trance, in this case

indicators.note: the shortened 'one is' goes inside the rearranged letters of the other word
a sort of trance is a reworked version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: One is I, and the 's is a shortened is, giving I + S

explanation.surface: Someone drifting into a kind of trance, as happens in this instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' rearranges TRANCE into CANTER, and 'in' puts IS (I for one, S for the 's) inside it after CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a small metal container, a kind of case for tea or film.

clue.text: Distinction awarded initially in Rome

parts.note: the honour's initials are the two middle letters of the Italian capital's name, so it is found 'initially in Rome'

explanation.walkthrough: The British honour is abbreviated OM, and OM sits inside rOMe; 'initially' points at the abbreviation, not at the first letter of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a British honour given by the monarch for outstanding achievement, a distinction awarded to few.

clue.text: Poor Baker's in an elevated state

indicators.note: a poor version of the words is a botched one, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word with its S kept as a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A struggling baker finds himself in a state of high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges BAKERS + AN; 'elevated state' reads as a mood but is a US state on the high plains.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state of the Great Plains rises steadily westward to the foothills of the Rockies, a high-lying state.

clue.text: Debauchee going to get share in spoils?

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man of loose living
off means leaving, as in 'I'm off'

explanation.surface: A dissolute man setting out to claim his part of the loot.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake-off is a commission or cut taken from the proceeds, often dishonestly.

clue.text: Wool from some farmer in Orkney ?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fleece produced by a sheep farmer on the Orkney islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Merino is a fine soft wool from the Spanish breed of sheep of that name.

clue.text: Victor appears to cling 'to love

parts.note: to hug is to cling to someone tightly
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A winner seems to be holding on tight to his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like a winner but is the first name of the French novelist Victor Hugo.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor is the forename of the French author of Les Misérables, whose surname this is.

clue.text: Borrow book from Vera Long, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the name might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A request to take out a volume on loan from a woman named Vera Long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borrow' looks like a verb but is George Borrow, the English writer of travel books.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the 1851 semi-autobiographical novel by George Borrow, so a book of his.

clue.text: Nymph appears so in area

indicators.note: the word for 'so' is placed in the middle of the word for area

parts.note: taken as written
thus means so, in this way

explanation.surface: A nymph shows up just like this in the district.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this nymph was changed into a spring to escape the river god Alpheus.

clue.text: She may return to take courses

indicators.note: returning means the word for eating a meal is read backwards

parts.note: to dine is to eat a meal of several courses

explanation.surface: A woman might come back to attend classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take courses' suggests study, but courses are parts of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name stands in for 'she', a female person.

clue.text: Means being out of employment ?

parts.note: 'out of employment' reads as jobless, but here means money coming out of, arising from, a job

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a person living on means while unemployed; the definition is money whose source is work.
explanation.definitionFit: This is income from wages or salary, money resulting from employment as opposed to investments.

clue.text: Rebuff joint offer' at board meeting ?

definitions.meaning: a cut of cold lamb or mutton served at the dining table

explanation.surface: A company's directors turn down a combined proposal at their meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board meeting' suggests directors, but the board is a dining table and the joint is meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A snub is called this after the cold meat once served to unwelcome guests, and the meat itself is a joint served at table.

clue.text: Condescends to take work on board, apparently

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, the steamship abbreviation

parts.note: SS is the steamship abbreviation, appearing as on board
taken as written
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone deigns to take on a job aboard ship, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoop is to lower oneself to do something beneath one, to deign.

clue.text: Nonsensical measure connected with fish

parts.note: a foot is a unit of length
ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: An absurd unit of length relating to fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Footling means trivial or silly, of no consequence.

clue.text: Walk heavily like a character in " The Virginian "

parts.note: to tramp is to walk with heavy steps
as means like, in the manner of

explanation.surface: A clumsy stride resembling a cowboy from a famous western.
explanation.walkthrough: The Virginian is Owen Wister's 1902 western novel, later a TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Trampas is the villain whom the hero confronts in Owen Wister's western novel.

clue.text: Leaves carrier-each entering the river

indicators.note: entering puts the word 'each' into the river's name

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, famous for trout fishing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A carrier of foliage, each one going into the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is a wooden box in which dried tea is shipped, a carrier for the leaves.

clue.text: Eminent executant in some art form

indicators.note: to form the letters is to shape them anew, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A distinguished performer working in a particular artistic medium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' looks like part of 'art form' but rearranges SOME ART.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished musician or conductor, a master performer.

clue.text: Vouch — for the. account — many tried arranging that!

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many

indicators.note: arranging the word puts its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone swears to the books, though many have tried to rig them.
explanation.definitionFit: To accredit is to give official backing to, to certify or vouch for.

clue.text: Natural phenomenon for Henry Higgins, plainly Spanish

definitions.text: Natural phenomenon for Henry Higgins, plainly Spanish

parts.words: Natural phenomenon for Henry Higgins, plainly Spanish
parts.note: recalls the elocution drill in My Fair Lady, where the weather in Spain stays mainly on the plain

explanation.walkthrough: Henry Higgins teaches Eliza the line 'The rain in Spain stays mainly in the plain'; 'plainly Spanish' points to that weather.
explanation.definitionFit: It is precipitation, water falling from clouds, a natural phenomenon.

clue.text: The poet we'd pick ?

definitions.meaning: Thomas ..., the Elizabethan poet and composer
a pink or white wild flower one might gather

explanation.walkthrough: The poet's surname is also the name of a wild flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas of that surname wrote lute songs, and the same word names a wild flower of the pink family.

clue.text: The course to go to Mars, for example ?

definitions.text: The course to go to Mars, for example ?

parts.words: The course to go to Mars, for example
parts.note: the course sounds like a space trajectory, but it is a meal course served to Mars, a god

explanation.walkthrough: Mars here is the Roman god of war, not the planet, and a course is food.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the food of the gods in classical myth, fit to serve to a deity.

clue.text: Understands a point in children's pastime

parts.note: sees means understands, as in 'I see'
W is a compass point, west

explanation.surface: Someone grasps the purpose of a game children play.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a plank balanced on a pivot that children ride up and down.

clue.text: Composer gets many, an offer of a lift ?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
'hop in' is what a driver says offering a ride

explanation.surface: A musician receives many offers of a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was the Polish Romantic composer of piano music.

clue.text: Animal springs to' view in Wordsworth's poem

parts.note: a hart is a male deer
to leap is to spring
a well is where water springs up to view

explanation.surface: A deer suddenly bounds into sight in a poem by Wordsworth.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem tells of a hunted hart's three leaps to its death beside a spring.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the 1800 Wordsworth poem about a spring marking where a hunted stag died.

clue.text: Out-and-out-row ?.

definitions.meaning: a line of soldiers or of taxis waiting

explanation.definitionFit: The word means utter or complete, and also a line of people or things, as in a taxi line.

clue.text: Give a hand in port

definitions.meaning: distribute cards to players in a game
a town on the Kent coast in England

explanation.surface: Lend assistance at the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a Kent coastal town; 'give a hand' means hand out cards, not help.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealers hand out cards, and the same name belongs to a coastal town in Kent.

clue.text: Capital gains to a manufacturer ?

indicators.note: a manufacturer makes something new from materials, so these letters are remade

explanation.surface: Profits on investments passing to an industrial firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital gains' reads as a tax phrase; Capital is the definition and 'manufacturer' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital city of Chile.

clue.text: Brown returns to mountains to make notes

indicators.note: returns means the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: tan is a light brown
the Urals are a mountain range in Russia

explanation.surface: Brown comes back to the mountains to write down some reminders.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a natural is a note neither sharp nor flat.
